LESSON: STORYTELLING LISTENING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Word and sentence By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners practice hearing 
Topic 1.3: Storytelling LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Storytelling LISTENING. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. develop vocabulary through listening to stories
2. show empathy with people, places, and things
3. recount key details of a story and retell it listened to

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. develop vocabulary through listening to stories
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to develop vocabulary through listening to stories. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. show empathy with people, places, and things
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to show empathy with people, places, and things. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. recount key details of a story and retell it listened to
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to recount key details of a story and retell it listened to. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Storytelling LISTENING.
2. Explain Storytelling LISTENING to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Storytelling LISTENING.
4. Show that you can: develop vocabulary through listening to stories
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Storytelling LISTENING. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Storytelling LISTENING important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. develop vocabulary through listening to stories
2. show empathy with people, places, and things
3. recount key details of a story and retell it listened to

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
